description.summary: A multimedia online horror narrative and alternate reality game by Alexander D. Hall ('Jadusable') begun on 4chan's /x/ board on 7 September 2010, framed as a haunted Nintendo 64 cartridge of The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask possessed by an entity called BEN.
description.full: BEN Drowned is a foundational creepypasta and alternate reality game (ARG) created by American writer Alexander D. Hall (online handle 'Jadusable'). It originally appeared as a thread titled 'Haunted Majora's Mask Cartridge' on 4chan's paranormal /x/ board on 7 September 2010, and unfolded as a daily multimedia serial through 15 September 2010. The story-within-the-story is told by 'Jadusable', a college sophomore who acquires a used Nintendo 64 cartridge of The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask (Nintendo, 2000) from an old man at a yard sale. The cartridge contains a save file named 'BEN'; subsequent gameplay sessions are recorded as YouTube videos showing increasingly glitched and uncanny behavior — Link being burned by the Happy Mask Salesman, the Elegy of Emptiness statue stalking the player, and the file repeatedly resetting itself. Through the in-fiction Cleverbot conversations and YouTube videos, an entity claims to be BEN, identified with a child who drowned. The narrative evolved into a multi-year ARG ('Moon Children', 'Arc 2: The Truth', etc.) and is widely considered one of the most influential works in the creepypasta genre, helping establish creepypasta as a recognized literary form. The series ran intermittently from 2010 to 2020.

etymology.origin: Coined by Alexander D. Hall in his 7 September 2010 4chan /x/ post; 'BEN' is the name of the save file on the haunted cartridge, and 'Drowned' is added because the in-fiction backstory (delivered through the haunted gameplay and Cleverbot dialogue) suggests BEN is the spirit of a boy who drowned.
etymology.meaning: Literal: a (fictional) boy named Ben who drowned, whose spirit haunts a Nintendo 64 cartridge.
etymology.first_use: 2010-09-07: 'Haunted Majora's Mask Cartridge' thread on 4chan's /x/ board (Alex Hall / Jadusable)

features.description: A grey N64 cartridge of The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask with the partly-rubbed-off name 'Majora' on the label and a save file named BEN
Link displayed in distorted, burned, or doubled forms; the Elegy of Emptiness statue moves toward the player
Songs from the original game played backward and at altered pitch in the haunted videos

physical.morphology: BEN exists in-fiction as a digital/haunting entity manifesting through a video game, YouTube videos, and online chat (Cleverbot) — not a corporeal being.

abilities.description: Inhabits and modifies a Nintendo 64 cartridge and its YouTube uploads
Hijacks Cleverbot conversations, replying with personal information and threats
Affects the protagonist's computer files, email, and (in later arcs) physical surroundings

patterns: Haunts a single target (Jadusable) across multiple platforms
Communicates via fragments of game text and reversed audio
Escalates from in-game oddities to direct online contact

range.description: Internet-native phenomenon; primarily distributed via 4chan's /x/ board, YouTube, and Jadusable's hosted website. Audience is global English-speaking internet users.
countries: Originating in the United States (Connecticut, where Hall was attending college)

origins.cultural_roots: Internet creepypasta culture of the late 2000s; 4chan /x/ paranormal discussion; the wider tradition of 'haunted video game' urban legends (e.g. the Lavender Town Pokémon legend).
origins.earliest_accounts: First post: 7 September 2010 on 4chan's /x/ board by user Jadusable (Alexander D. Hall), titled 'Haunted Majora's Mask Cartridge'.
origins.folklore_connections: Part of a wave of late-2000s/early-2010s online folklore that included Slender Man (2009), the Marble Hornets ARG (2009), and the broader creepypasta tradition.

timeline.event: Alex Hall posts the first 'Haunted Majora's Mask Cartridge' thread on 4chan's /x/ board, with the first YouTube video
End of the initial daily serialization (Day 4 / 'final' post)
timeline.significance: Closes the original arc as it appeared on 4chan

timeline.event: Expansion into a multi-arc ARG, including the 'Moon Children' storyline
timeline.significance: Transition from creepypasta to alternate reality game

timeline.event: Tenth-anniversary closing chapter posted by Hall

history.modern_era: BEN Drowned is treated by folklorists and game scholars as a paradigmatic example of digital folklore and online urban legend. It is studied alongside Slender Man as a major work in establishing creepypasta as a literary form. The story has been adapted into countless YouTube retellings, fan fiction, and merchandise; reference works in folkloristics and digital media studies discuss it as a canonical case of internet legend.

video.name: Jadusable YouTube videos (Sept 2010)
video.description: Series of YouTube videos uploaded by Jadusable showing the alleged haunted Majora's Mask cartridge.
video.analysis: Created by Alex Hall using a real but unmodified copy of Majora's Mask combined with editing, reversed audio, and game-engine glitches. The videos are intentional fiction; their effects are pre-planned.

documentary.name: Original 4chan /x/ thread, 7 September 2010
documentary.description: The original 'Haunted Majora's Mask Cartridge' thread on 4chan's /x/ paranormal board.
documentary.analysis: Foundational document; preserved via 4chan archives and Jadusable Wiki.

paranormal.name: In-fiction haunted-cartridge premise
paranormal.description: Within the narrative, BEN is the spirit of a drowned boy who possesses a Majora's Mask cartridge and pursues its owner through digital media.
evidence_cited: The series of videos and posts presenting the haunting

skeptical.name: Authored creepypasta / ARG
skeptical.description: BEN Drowned is a deliberately crafted multimedia fiction by Alexander D. Hall; the 'haunting' is a combination of editing, reversed audio, gameplay glitching, and ARG-style cross-platform staging. Hall has confirmed authorship publicly.
evidence_cited: Sustained narrative structure across multiple platforms

stories: The old man and the haunted cartridge
folklore.beliefs: Recognized in academic and journalistic treatments as a signal example of how internet communities co-author and transmit modern folklore.

literature: Trevor J. Blank & Lynne S. McNeill (eds.), Slender Man Is Coming (2018) — discusses creepypasta context including BEN Drowned
games: Numerous fan games and ROM hacks built around BEN imagery
other: Subject of academic articles in folkloristics and game studies
Frequently discussed in horror and gaming media coverage of creepypasta

researchers.contribution: Folklorist of digital legend, including creepypasta

research.ongoing_studies: BEN Drowned is a recurring case study in folkloristics, game studies, and the study of alternate reality games. Articles continue to appear in journals like Western Folklore and New Directions in Folklore.
